thread:
Alex W: Heads-up — noticed a surge in pod rebuilds this morning when spot GPUs in us-west2 get termination notices. Latency for warmup jumps, and some drains are taking >2m which is killing throughput.
Samir: What metrics are spiking? node drain time, kube-scheduler backoff, or just autoscaler churn?
Jenny (oncall): Node events show repeated TerminationNotice then kubelet Drain failed: timed out. Autoscaler reacted: scaled gpu-spot-pool +4, but because we had no warm spare on on-demand the jobs queued.
infra-bot: Autoscaler event: group gpu-spot-pool scaled 8 -> 12 to satisfy pending pods (policy: least-waste).
Tomas: Can we make evictions faster by setting safe-to-evict annotations and reducing PodDisruptionBudget windows? For training jobs we can be more aggressive.
Alex W: Two immediate levers I want to propose: 1) split gpu pool into spot (best-effort) and ondemand-warm (min 1-2 nodes) with labels and nodeAffinity fallback, 2) add a light termination handler that pre-caches KV/params to S3 so restarts are cheaper.
Samir: Agree on split. Also we should use a NoExecute taint for spot nodes so only tolerant pods land there. Example taint: `node.kubernetes.io/spot=true:NoExecute`. Tolerations on cheap/batch pods only.
Jenny (oncall): FYI our current CA config uses mixed-instance-pool but no nodeGroup priority. If we annotate the on-demand group with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/priority=100` CA will prefer ondemand for scale-up in critical times.
Tomas: Also add NodeLifecycleHook to run `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` from termination handler, and reduce drain timeout from default 10m to 90s for spot nodes. Quick snippet we tested:```bash
# termination-handler pre-drain
kubectl annotate node $NODE safe-to-evict=true
kubectl cordon $NODE
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30 --timeout=90s
```
Samir: Need caution: set lower grace-period only for jobs that support checkpointing. For stateful services keep normal window. Use node labels `gpu.workload=checkpointable` to target.
Alex W: Also proposal: enable continuous prefix caching for large models so a restart doesn't re-stream the whole KV. That reduces recovery latency by ~40%. That's more infra work but helps cost.
Jenny (oncall): Immediate action items I can do today: 1) create on-demand warm pool with min-size=1 and label `gpu.priority=ondemand`, 2) add taint on spot group and update tolerations on batch jobs, 3) push CA group priority annotation. Will monitor effects.
Tomas: I'll open a short runbook for the termination-handler flow and add a canary. Also suggest adding a short-lived preemptible eviction metric in Grafana: `spot.eviction.cooldown_seconds` to track time-between-evictions.
Samir: SGTM. Long term: think about autoscaler expander policy and a fallback policy that prefers a cheaper region before bursting on-demand in the same region. But that's a follow-up.
Alex W: Perfect. Jenny, assign a PR for the CA and node group changes and tag me. If we see repeated >3 evictions per hour we consider raising base ondemand min. :thumbsup:
